summary: The learning crisis is particularly acute in areas where teacher quality is low and electricity is unreliable. A paper-and-pencil-based individualised self-learning programme in Dhaka's disadvantaged communities made children markedly faster and more accurate at math problem sol…

title: The hidden cost of disruptive classmates on test scores
summary: A field experiment in Ecuador finds that a small number of children with persistent behavioural problems lower the achievement of their classmates. The effects are larger for younger children, increase with the number of poorly behaved children in the classroom, and persist for…

title: Using government data to study private sector growth
summary: Government tax records reveal how firms influence one another – from VAT evasion uncovered through mismatched returns in Uganda to productivity gains that spread along supply chains when Turkish manufacturers adopt industrial robots.

title: How a 30-minute session with medical professionals nearly tripled organ donor registration
summary: Thousands die each year waiting for an organ transplant. In Tunisia, one expert-led classroom session tripled student donor registrations.

title: Corruption in public procurement: How politicians co-opt bureaucrats
summary: Why do politicians steer public contracts to party loyalists, and how do they get professional bureaucrats to go along? Evidence from Ghana, India, and Indonesia shows that merit-based hiring is only the first step in tackling corruption in public procurement.

title: How bureaucratic incentives drive the fight against air pollution
summary: Local officials in China work harder on air quality when the target is doomed to fail, but relax their efforts when it is secured early, revealing how minimum standards shape bureaucratic effort when they are also judged on economic growth.

title: No taxation without administration: What makes tax authorities work
summary: New research argues that how tax authorities are organised, staffed, and managed matters as much as tax policy itself, offering developing countries a powerful lever for raising revenue even where third-party data is scarce.

title: Who gets what? Budgets and discretion in community-led social protection targeting
summary: In Ethiopia, community leaders tasked with selection of beneficiaries for social assistance prioritised coverage over transfer size when budgets were cut, while discretion allowed them to reach poor and conflict-affected households.

title: Proximity over pay: Why small towns attract migrants
summary: Because rural migrants are deterred far more by distance than they are drawn by higher pay, nearby towns – despite offering lower earnings than cities – end up absorbing far more migrants and doing more to reduce poverty, making them a decisive channel for inclusive urban growth.

title: Rethinking development cooperation: The case for a ‘balance sheet’ approach
summary: As global aid budgets shrink, the Future of Development Cooperation Coalition proposes a 'development balance sheet' that reframes low- and middle-income countries not as aid recipients but as economic actors managing their own assets and liabilities.
